
Two arXiv papers from the RSS feed have strong harness-layer relevance. The 'Tool-Use Tax' paper provides empirical evidence that tool dispatch overhead measurably impacts agent performance — directly addressing harness design tradeoffs. The 'To Call or Not to Call' paper proposes a framework for optimizing tool-calling decisions at the harness layer. Grok social signals were mostly duplicates or application-level frameworks not meeting the inclusion bar.

## Suggestions

- [Are Tools All We Need? Unveiling the Tool-Use Tax in LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00136) — Empirical study quantifying the performance overhead ('tool-use tax') introduced by harness-layer tool dispatch, providing evidence that harness design choices directly affect agent reliability and efficiency.
  Section: Research Papers > Tool & API Integration Layers | Criteria: Manages tool dispatch, context handling, state management, or safety constraints at the harness layer, Empirical or production evidence of harness design improving reliability, safety, or performance, Evaluates or benchmarks agent behavior through controlled harness-mediated interactions

- [To Call or Not to Call: A Framework to Assess and Optimize LLM Tool Calling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00737) — Proposes a harness-layer framework for deciding when agents should invoke tools, optimizing tool dispatch decisions to reduce unnecessary calls and improve execution reliability.
  Section: Research Papers > Tool & API Integration Layers | Criteria: Manages tool dispatch, context handling, state management, or safety constraints at the harness layer, Defines or implements the execution loop, scaffolding, or runtime environment that hosts an AI agent, Evaluates or benchmarks agent behavior through controlled harness-mediated interactions
